name: Virtual call versus dynamic_cast microbenchmark (Chapter 1 example)
listed_description: Google Benchmark comparison of a virtual function call against dynamic_cast from Base* to Derived*; the book suggests a virtual type() tag when a fast type check is needed.
claim_text: About 1 nanosecond for the virtual call, 5 to 10 nanoseconds for the dynamic cast; absolute numbers depend on hardware.
book_benchmark: Google Benchmark, one Base/Derived hierarchy, p->f() timed against dynamic_cast<Derived*>(p). Compiler, flags and CPU not stated in this chunk. The virtual type-tag alternative is shown as code, not timed.
found_in: book: Hands-On Design Patterns with C++, 2nd ed. (2023), ch. 1, Polymorphism and virtual functions (dynamic cast cost); code in companion repo Chapter01

name: scoped_ptr and std::unique_ptr dereference versus raw pointer (Chapter 5 Example 07)
listed_description: Google Benchmark showing a hand-written scoped_ptr and std::unique_ptr dereference at the same speed as a raw pointer (zero-overhead RAII).
claim_text: Raw pointer 3.42 ns, scoped_ptr 3.37 ns, unique_ptr 3.42 ns per 32-dereference iteration: smart pointers incur no overhead.
book_benchmark: Google Benchmark, REPEAT(DoNotOptimize(*p)) x32 per iteration, items_per_second about 9.4G/s; built with -O3 --std=c++17 per the book's sample command. CPU not stated. Parity result, not a speedup.
found_in: book: Hands-On Design Patterns with C++, 2nd ed. (2023), ch. 5, A Comprehensive Look at RAII, section The RAII idiom / RAII in a nutshell; code in companion repo Chapter05

name: Type-erased deleter versus template and explicit delete (Chapter 6 benchmark)
listed_description: Benchmark table shown in the Preface as a sample of console output, timing explicit delete, a type-erased deleter, a faster type-erased variant and a template deleter; full discussion is in the type erasure chapter (later chunk).
claim_text: BM_delete_explicit 4.54 ns, BM_delete_type_erased 13.4 ns, BM_delete_type_erased_fast 12.7 ns, BM_delete_template 4.56 ns.
book_benchmark: Google Benchmark, delete of an object through four deleter styles; compiler, flags and CPU not stated in this chunk. The table appears only as a formatting example in the Conventions section.
found_in: book: Hands-On Design Patterns with C++, 2nd ed. (2023), Preface, Conventions used (console output sample); chapter 6 Understanding Type Erasure covers it
